title: Finite biproduct equivalence for unconditional curve assertions
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, $k$ a field, $X$ a scheme and $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$.
Let $I$ be a finite index type and $G_a$ module sheaves on the small etale site of $X$.
Let $H$ be a module sheaf equipped with an isomorphism $e:H\simeq\bigoplus_a G_a$,
using finite biproducts [def-weil-additive-category]. The predicates $C_1,\ldots,C_8$
are those of [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions], with their stated conditional hypotheses.
Assume each $G_a$ and $H$ is constructible [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. Then
$(C_1(H)\land C_2(H)\land C_5(H)\land C_7(H)\land C_8(H))$ holds if and only if
$C_1(G_a)\land C_2(G_a)\land C_5(G_a)\land C_7(G_a)\land C_8(G_a)$ holds for every $a$.
There is no prime annihilator hypothesis.

source.place: Theorem 03SC, proof, fourth paragraph; Lemma 0A5C. Primary text checked at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03SC and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A5C.

proof.text: Taking underlying abelian sheaves is additive by reflexivity, and Sheaf.functorH is additive. For their composite F, identify F(H) with the product of F(G i) using F.mapIso(e), Functor.mapBiproduct and AddCommGrpCat.biproductIsoPi. The coordinate at i is F.map(e.hom composed with biproduct.π G i). This is a product equivalence also for the empty index type. Subsingleton and finiteness are equivalent to their coordinatewise versions: evaluation is surjective because every factor contains zero; conversely products of subsingletons are subsingletons and finite products of finite types are finite.

For any scheme map a and degree q, form the natural transformation with components Etale.cohomologyMap a (-) q from the underlying-sheaf cohomology functor to its inverse-image counterpart. Both functors are additive; naturality is the existing Etale.cohomologyMap_map. In the product coordinates, surjectivity implies surjectivity of each factor by lifting a vector supported at that factor, and the converse follows by choosing coordinate preimages. Injectivity implies factorwise injectivity because each summand has injection biproduct.ι G i composed with e.inv, retracted by e.hom composed with biproduct.π G i, and the square commutes by naturality. The converse follows by the joint injectivity of coordinates. Combine injectivity and surjectivity for bijectivity.

Unfold C1, C2, C5, C7 and C8 and apply the coordinatewise tests degree by degree. For C2 and C7 the affine or proper instance is shared. For C5 use the assumed constructibility of H in the forward direction and hGc i in the reverse direction; no constructibility-of-biproduct theorem is required. Assemble the five implications into the stated equivalence by introducing or projecting the five conjunctions.

proof_origin.place: Q2 Lean proof of the finite-sum argument in Theorem 03SC, fourth paragraph; Lemma 0A5C. Uses the existing Ext-based functor and naturality API directly.

lean.statement:
theorem prime_biproduct_unconditional_iff (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ]
    {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    {ι : Type} [Finite ι]
    (G : ι → Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ))
    (hGc : ∀ a, Scheme.IsConstructibleSheaf (G a))
    {H : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)} (e : H ≅ ⨁ G)
    (hHc : Scheme.IsConstructibleSheaf H) :
    (VanishingAboveTwo Λ H ∧ VanishingAboveOneOfIsAffine Λ H ∧
      FiniteOfIsProper Λ f H ∧ BaseChangeOfIsProper Λ f H ∧
      SurjectiveRestrictionTwo Λ H) ↔
      ∀ a, VanishingAboveTwo Λ (G a) ∧ VanishingAboveOneOfIsAffine Λ (G a) ∧
        FiniteOfIsProper Λ f (G a) ∧ BaseChangeOfIsProper Λ f (G a) ∧
        SurjectiveRestrictionTwo Λ (G a)
